layers.name: ext4 Filesystem
layers.description: How files are organized on disk

steps.title: Command Execution
steps.description: User runs a command like `echo "Hello" > file.txt`. The shell parses the command and prepares to create the file.
steps.simpleDescription: You type a command to create a file
steps.kernelDetails: Shell parses command, handles redirections, prepares syscalls
steps.hardwareDetails: Keyboard input → terminal → shell process

steps.title: Open File Request
steps.description: The program calls `open()` with O_CREAT flag. This triggers a syscall to enter kernel mode.
steps.simpleDescription: Program asks kernel to create a new file
steps.kernelDetails: syscall instruction → do_sys_open() → path_openat()
steps.hardwareDetails: CPU switches from user mode (ring 3) to kernel mode (ring 0)

steps.title: Path Resolution
steps.description: Kernel walks the directory tree to find where the new file should be created. Checks permissions along the way.
steps.simpleDescription: Kernel finds the parent directory and checks permissions
steps.kernelDetails: link_path_walk() traverses dentry cache, inode_permission() checks access
steps.hardwareDetails: Usually cached in RAM — no disk access needed

steps.title: Allocate Inode
steps.description: ext4 finds a free inode (metadata structure) and initializes it with file attributes: permissions, owner, timestamps.
steps.simpleDescription: Kernel reserves space for file metadata
steps.kernelDetails: ext4_new_inode() scans inode bitmap, marks inode as used
steps.hardwareDetails: Inode bitmap update will be written to SSD

steps.title: Add Directory Entry
steps.description: The new filename is added to the parent directory, linking the name to the allocated inode number.
steps.simpleDescription: Directory now knows the new file exists
steps.kernelDetails: ext4_add_entry() updates parent directory block or htree index
steps.hardwareDetails: Directory block will be written to SSD

steps.title: Journal Transaction
steps.description: Before writing to disk, ext4 logs the metadata changes to the journal. This ensures crash consistency — if power fails, the journal can replay or rollback.
steps.simpleDescription: Changes are logged for crash safety
steps.kernelDetails: jbd2_journal_start() → journal metadata → jbd2_journal_commit_transaction()
steps.hardwareDetails: Journal written sequentially to SSD for speed

steps.title: File Created
steps.description: The file now exists! Kernel returns a file descriptor to the program. The file appears in directory listings.
steps.simpleDescription: File is now visible and usable
steps.kernelDetails: dentry_open() creates file object, get_unused_fd() returns fd to userspace
steps.hardwareDetails: Metadata now persisted on SSD

steps.title: Write Request
steps.description: Program calls `write(fd, data, size)` to write content to the file.
steps.simpleDescription: Program writes data to the file
steps.kernelDetails: ksys_write() → vfs_write() → file's write operation
steps.hardwareDetails: Data still in user-space memory

steps.title: Copy to Page Cache
steps.description: Kernel copies data from user memory into the page cache — RAM pages that temporarily hold file contents. Pages are marked 'dirty' (need writing to disk).
steps.simpleDescription: Data copied to kernel's memory cache
steps.kernelDetails: __filemap_get_folio() allocates pages, _copy_from_user() copies data
steps.hardwareDetails: Data now in RAM, not yet on SSD

steps.title: Allocate Data Blocks
steps.description: ext4 reserves disk blocks for the file data and updates the extent tree to map file offsets to disk locations.
steps.simpleDescription: Disk space reserved for file data
steps.kernelDetails: ext4_map_blocks() allocates blocks, updates extent tree
steps.hardwareDetails: Block bitmap and extent metadata will be updated

steps.title: Writeback Begins
steps.description: Background kernel threads notice dirty pages and start writing them to disk. In data=ordered mode, data is written before metadata is committed.
steps.simpleDescription: Background process starts saving to disk
steps.kernelDetails: ext4_writepages() generates bios for dirty pages
steps.hardwareDetails: Data flows through block layer to SSD

steps.title: Block Layer Processing
steps.description: The block layer organizes write requests into bios, merges adjacent requests, and submits them to the NVMe driver via multiple hardware queues.
steps.simpleDescription: I/O requests organized and queued
steps.kernelDetails: submit_bio() → blk-mq → I/O scheduler (mq-deadline or none)
steps.hardwareDetails: Multiple queue pairs enable parallel I/O submission

steps.title: NVMe Command Submission
steps.description: NVMe driver places WRITE commands on submission queues. The SSD controller reads these via PCIe and processes them.
steps.simpleDescription: Commands sent to SSD over PCIe
steps.kernelDetails: nvme_queue_rq() builds commands, rings doorbell register
steps.hardwareDetails: PCIe Gen4: ~7GB/s bandwidth, sub-10µs latency

steps.title: SSD Processing
steps.description: The SSD's Flash Translation Layer (FTL) maps logical block addresses to physical NAND pages, applies error correction, and programs the flash cells.
steps.simpleDescription: SSD writes data to flash memory
steps.kernelDetails: Transparent to kernel — SSD appears as simple block device
steps.hardwareDetails: FTL handles wear leveling, garbage collection, bad block management

steps.title: NAND Programming
steps.description: NAND flash cells are electrically programmed. Each page (16KB typical) takes ~100-500µs to write. The FTL may batch multiple writes together.
steps.simpleDescription: Data stored in flash memory cells
steps.kernelDetails: N/A — this is internal to SSD
steps.hardwareDetails: NAND cells store charge representing 1-4 bits per cell (SLC/MLC/TLC/QLC)

steps.title: I/O Completion
steps.description: SSD signals completion via interrupt. NVMe driver processes completion queue entries, and the block layer marks the bio as complete.
steps.simpleDescription: SSD confirms write is done
steps.kernelDetails: NVMe interrupt → blk_mq_complete_request() → bio_endio()
steps.hardwareDetails: Completion queue entry written by SSD, read by driver

steps.title: Pages Marked Clean
steps.description: After successful writeback, dirty pages in the page cache are marked clean. They can now be freed or reused.
steps.simpleDescription: Memory cache updated to reflect disk state
steps.kernelDetails: end_buffer_async_write() or end_page_writeback() clears dirty flags
steps.hardwareDetails: Data now safely on SSD

steps.title: Metadata Commit
steps.description: ext4 commits the journal transaction for metadata (inode size, extent updates). This ensures the file's metadata is consistent with its data.
steps.simpleDescription: File metadata saved with crash guarantee
steps.kernelDetails: jbd2_journal_commit_transaction() writes commit block
steps.hardwareDetails: Journal commit is sequential write for performance

steps.title: fsync() Ensures Durability
steps.description: If the program calls fsync(), kernel ensures all data and metadata are on stable storage before returning. This guarantees the file survives power loss.
steps.simpleDescription: Program can ensure data is safely stored
steps.kernelDetails: ext4_sync_file() flushes data and commits journal
steps.hardwareDetails: May trigger cache flush commands to SSD

steps.title: TRIM for Deleted Blocks
steps.description: When files are deleted or fstrim runs, the kernel sends TRIM/DISCARD commands to the SSD, allowing it to reclaim unused blocks for better performance and longevity.
steps.simpleDescription: SSD can reclaim space from deleted files
steps.kernelDetails: blkdev_issue_discard() → NVMe DEALLOCATE command
steps.hardwareDetails: FTL marks physical blocks as erasable, improving write performance
